stories.headline: Bessent and Powell Summon Bank CEOs to Warn of Cyber Risks From Anthropic's Mythos Model

key_facts.fact: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Fed Chair Jerome Powell convened an urgent meeting with bank CEOs at Treasury headquarters in Washington on Tuesday to warn of cyber risks posed by Anthropic's Mythos model.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell convened an urgent meeting with bank CEOs this week to warn of cyber risks posed by Anthropic's latest AI model.

key_facts.fact: CEOs of Citigroup, Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and Goldman Sachs were present; JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon was unable to join.
key_facts.excerpt: Bloomberg News, which first reported the matter on Thursday, said the CEOs of Citigroup, Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and Goldman Sachs were present. JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon was unable to join.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said Mythos is capable of identifying and exploiting weaknesses across 'every major operating system and every major web browser,' detecting thousands of high- and critical-severity bugs, some undiscovered for decades.
key_facts.excerpt: Mythos' AI programming is able to find potential weaknesses in cybersecurity, and it can 'detect thousands of high- and critical-severity bugs and software defects, with vulnerabilities identified in most major operating systems and web browsers.' Some of these vulnerabilities 'had been undiscovered for decades.'

key_facts.fact: Access to Mythos will be limited to about 40 technology companies, including Microsoft and Google; Anthropic does not plan to release the model to the general public.
key_facts.excerpt: Access to Mythos will be limited to about 40 technology companies, including Microsoft and Google, the startup has said.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic proactively briefed senior U.S. government officials and key industry stakeholders on Mythos's capabilities ahead of its release, including ongoing discussions about the model's 'offensive and defensive cyber capabilities.'
key_facts.excerpt: A third source close to the matter reiterated Anthropic's outreach, saying the company proactively briefed senior U.S. government officials and key industry stakeholders on Mythos's capabilities ahead of its release.

key_facts.fact: The tech firms with access are expected to use Mythos under Project Glasswing to hunt for flaws in their products and share findings with industry peers — the first time a leading AI lab has built a frontier model and decided the public cannot use it.
key_facts.excerpt: The tech firms are expected to use Mythos as part of a project called Glasswing to 'hunt for flaws in their products and share findings with industry peers.' It is a notable change because it will be the 'first time a leading AI lab has built a frontier model and simultaneously decided the public cannot use it.'

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches $100/Month ChatGPT Pro Tier as Codex Hits 3 Million Weekly Users

key_facts.fact: OpenAI introduced a new $100/month ChatGPT Pro subscription tier positioned between the $20 Plus plan and the existing $200 Pro plan, focused on heavier Codex usage.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, the firm arguably most synonymous with the generative AI boom announced it will begin offering a new, more mid-range subscription tier — a $100 ChatGPT Pro plan — which joins its free, Go ($8 monthly), Plus ($20 monthly) and existing Pro ($200 monthly) plans.

key_facts.fact: The new tier offers 5x more Codex usage than Plus, with a temporary promotional boost to 10x through May 31, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The new $100/month Pro tier provides 5x more Codex usage than the $20/month ChatGPT Plus plan. Through May 31, customers who subscribe to the $100/month Pro plan will get up to 10x usage of ChatGPT Plus on Codex.

key_facts.fact: Codex now has over 3 million weekly users, growing 5x in three months with around 70% month-on-month growth.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI says Codex now has over 3 million weekly users, growing 5x in just three months with around 70% month-on-month growth.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is simultaneously 'rebalancing' Codex usage in the $20 Plus plan to support more sessions across the week rather than longer single-day sessions.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI's official company account on X noted that 'we're rebalancing Codex usage in Plus to support more sessions throughout the week, rather than longer sessions in a single day.'

key_facts.fact: Pro subscribers get access to GPT-5.4 Pro for advanced reasoning, unlimited GPT-5.3 usage, faster image generation, and expanded capabilities for agent-style tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: Users get access to GPT-5.4 Pro for advanced reasoning, maximum Codex task limits, and expanded memory and context handling. OpenAI is also offering unlimited GPT-5.3 usage, faster and unlimited image generation, and support for deep research and agent mode.

stories.headline: Anthropic Makes Claude Cowork Generally Available With Enterprise Controls and Zoom Integration

key_facts.fact: Claude Cowork, previously a research preview, is now generally available to all paid Anthropic plans (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise) on macOS and Windows.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has announced the general availability of Claude Cowork for all paid plans, expanding its reach to a broad spectrum of business teams beyond engineering.

key_facts.fact: Six enterprise features were added: role-based access controls, group spend limits, usage analytics, expanded OpenTelemetry support, a Zoom MCP connector, and per-tool connector controls.
key_facts.excerpt: Starting today, Claude Cowork includes six features built especially for enterprise use: Role-based access controls, Group spend limits, Usage analytics, Expanded OpenTelemetry support, Zoom MCP connector, Per tool connector controls.

key_facts.fact: Claude Cowork uses the same agentic architecture that powers Claude Code, enabling complex multi-step tasks with direct local file access and sub-agent coordination, now without requiring the terminal.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Cowork uses the same agentic architecture that powers Claude Code, now accessible within Claude Desktop and without opening the terminal. Instead of responding to prompts one at a time, Claude can take on complex, multi-step tasks and execute them on your behalf.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic launched Cowork as a research preview 12 weeks ago; since then millions have adopted it and hundreds of thousands more try it weekly, according to Felix Rieseberg at Anthropic.
key_facts.excerpt: We released Claude Cowork as a research preview 12 weeks ago. Since then, millions of people have made it part of how they work - and hundreds of thousands more are trying it every week.

key_facts.fact: PayPal is among early enterprise adopters rolling out Cowork across teams, with a joint webinar planned for April 16 on deployment best practices.
key_facts.excerpt: You'll also hear from PayPal on how they're rolling Cowork out across their teams — what's working, what they're watching, and how these controls have shaped their deployment plan.

stories.headline: Anthropic Explores Designing Own AI Chips as Revenue Run Rate Surpasses $30 Billion

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is in preliminary stages of evaluating in-house chip development, but has no formal commitment, finalized design, or dedicated team in place yet.
key_facts.excerpt: Reuters is citing sources that say Anthropic is looking closely at the possibility of building its own chips, amid industry concerns that the supply of sophisticated chips required for new AI systems may not keep pace.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate has surged past $30 billion, up from roughly $9 billion at the end of 2025, and more than 1,000 business customers spend over $1M annualized, doubling in less than two months.
key_facts.excerpt: According to the company, revenue run rate has already surpassed $30bn, up from around $9bn at the end of 2025. More than 1,000 of Anthropic's business customers spend more than $1m on an annualised basis, doubling in less than two months.

key_facts.fact: Earlier this week, Anthropic announced an expanded agreement to tap 3.5GW of Google TPU capacity from Broadcom, expected to come online in 2027, building on last October's deal worth 'tens of billions of dollars' for 1 million TPUs.
key_facts.excerpt: Earlier this week, Anthropic announced a new expanded agreement that will allow Anthropic to tap 3.5GW of Google's tensor processing unit (TPU) capacity from Broadcom. The multi-gigawatt capacity is expected to come online in 2027.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic captures more than 73% of all spending among companies buying AI tools for the first time, while OpenAI's share has dropped to around 27%.
key_facts.excerpt: Recent data shows that Anthropic is now capturing more than 73pc of all spending among companies buying AI tools for the first time, while its rival OpenAI is down to around 27pc.

key_facts.fact: Designing advanced AI chips is estimated to cost as high as $500 million; rivals Meta and OpenAI already have custom chip projects underway.
key_facts.excerpt: Designing advanced AI chips is both complex and costly, with estimates suggesting development can run as high as $500 million.

stories.headline: xAI Sues Colorado to Block AI Anti-Discrimination Law, Citing First Amendment Violations

key_facts.fact: xAI filed a federal lawsuit against Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser to block enforcement of a 2024 state law requiring 'high-risk' AI system developers to protect consumers against 'algorithmic discrimination' in education, employment, housing, and other sectors.
key_facts.excerpt: The company, xAI, filed a lawsuit against Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser (D) on Thursday, seeking to block enforcement of a 2024 law that requires developers of 'high-risk' systems to protect consumers against 'algorithmic discrimination' in education, employment, housing and other sectors.

key_facts.fact: xAI argues the law violates the First Amendment by prohibiting AI developers from 'producing speech that the State of Colorado dislikes' and compelling them to 'conform their speech to a State-enforced orthodoxy on controversial topics.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Its provisions prohibit developers of AI systems from producing speech that the State of Colorado dislikes, while compelling them to conform their speech to a State-enforced orthodoxy on controversial topics of great public concern,' the lawsuit states.

key_facts.fact: Colorado was the first U.S. state to pass a comprehensive AI regulation bill; Governor Jared Polis signed it 'with reservations' and the law was delayed from February to June 30 to take effect.
key_facts.excerpt: Colorado earned a distinction in 2024 when it became the first state in the country to pass a comprehensive AI regulation bill. Governor Jared Polis, a Democrat, signed the bill but made his discomfort public, noting he did so 'with reservations.' The law was originally supposed to take effect in February but was delayed until June 30.

key_facts.fact: xAI is seeking a court injunction to halt enforcement plus a formal declaration that the legislation is unconstitutional.
key_facts.excerpt: The lawsuit was filed in U.S. district court in Colorado. xAI is asking the court for an injunction to halt enforcement of the law, along with a formal declaration that the legislation is unconstitutional.

key_facts.fact: The lawsuit comes amid a broader fight between states drafting AI rules and the Trump administration pushing for a single federal framework, with Trump writing on Truth Social: 'There must be only One Rulebook if we are going to continue to lead in AI.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'There must be only One Rulebook if we are going to continue to lead in AI,' President Trump wrote on Truth Social.

stories.headline: Jassy Says AWS AI Revenue Hits $15B Run Rate, Amazon Custom Chips Now at $20B+

key_facts.fact: AWS's AI revenue run rate has reached over $15 billion as of Q1 2026, up from essentially nothing three years ago, according to Andy Jassy's annual shareholder letter.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon Web Services' AI business is on pace to book $15 billion in annual revenue, up from essentially nothing three years ago.

key_facts.fact: Amazon's three custom silicon lines — Graviton, Trainium, and Nitro — produce over $20 billion in annualized revenue, growing at triple-digit rates YoY; Jassy estimates the business would be worth ~$50 billion if sold externally.
key_facts.excerpt: Our annual revenue run rate for our chips business (inclusive of Graviton, Trainium, and Nitro) is now over $20 billion, and growing triple digit percentages YoY. If our chips business was a stand-alone business, and sold chips produced this year to AWS and other third parties, our annual run rate would be ~$50 billion.

key_facts.fact: Amazon plans to spend approximately $200 billion in capital expenditures in 2026, primarily on AI infrastructure; Jassy wrote 'We're not investing approximately $200 billion in capex in 2026 on a hunch.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'We're not investing approximately $200 billion in capex in 2026 on a hunch,' Jassy wrote. 'We're not going to be conservative in how we play this.'

key_facts.fact: Jassy said using Trainium at scale will 'save tens of billions of capex dollars per year, and provide several hundred basis points of operating margin advantage versus relying on others' chips for inference.'
key_facts.excerpt: He estimated that by using its own Trainium chips at scale, the company will 'save tens of billions of capex dollars per year, and provide several hundred basis points of operating margin advantage versus relying on others' chips for inference.'

key_facts.fact: Amazon's total revenue grew 12% YoY to $717 billion in 2025 with $80 billion operating income, but free cash flow fell from $38 billion to $11 billion due to heavy AI infrastructure spending.
key_facts.excerpt: On the top line, Amazon closed 2025 at $717 billion, having expanded sales by 12% from the $638 billion recorded in 2024. Operating income rose 17% to $80 billion.

key_facts.fact: Jassy pointed to a deal with OpenAI worth more than $100 billion as a signal of AI demand backing Amazon's spending plans.
key_facts.excerpt: Jassy pointed to a deal with OpenAI worth more than $100 billion as a signal of the kind of demand his company is banking on.

stories.headline: Florida Attorney General Launches Investigation Into OpenAI Over FSU Shooting and Child Safety

key_facts.fact: Florida AG James Uthmeier launched an investigation into OpenAI and ChatGPT, citing national security concerns, alleged links to criminal behavior, and ChatGPT's role in the April 2025 Florida State University mass shooting that killed two.
key_facts.excerpt: Florida's attorney general, James Uthmeier, announced Thursday that his office planned to investigate OpenAI over the alleged role of ChatGPT in a deadly shooting last year. In April 2025, a gunman opened fire on Florida State University's campus, killing two and injuring five.

key_facts.fact: Uthmeier said subpoenas to OpenAI are 'forthcoming' and raised concerns about OpenAI's data falling 'into the hands of America's enemies, such as the Chinese Communist Party.'
key_facts.excerpt: In a video posted to X, Uthmeier said there were concerns about whether OpenAI's data and AI technologies could fall 'into the hands of America's enemies, such as the Chinese Communist Party.' Subpoenas to the company will be issued shortly.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said it will cooperate, noting ChatGPT has over 900 million weekly active users and the company builds it 'to understand people's intent and respond in a safe and appropriate way.'
key_facts.excerpt: An OpenAI spokesperson provided the following statement: 'Each week, more than 900 million people use ChatGPT to improve their daily lives... We build ChatGPT to understand people's intent and respond in a safe and appropriate way, and we continue improving our technology. We will cooperate with the Attorney General's investigation.'

key_facts.fact: The probe comes as OpenAI prepares for an IPO that could value it at up to $1 trillion.
key_facts.excerpt: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier on Thursday launched an investigation into OpenAI and its chatbot ChatGPT, as the artificial intelligence firm prepares for an IPO that could value it at up to $1 trillion.

key_facts.fact: The family of shooting victim Robert Morales plans to sue OpenAI; attorneys claim the shooter 'was in constant communication' with ChatGPT leading up to the attack.
key_facts.excerpt: The family of 57-year-old Robert Morales, who was killed in the FSU shooting, reportedly plans to sue OpenAI over ChatGPT's role in his death.
